newsitem.title: INDIA: India president consults leaders on new government.
newsitem.headline: India president consults leaders on new government.

text.p: Indian President Shankar Dayal Sharma met the leaders of three political groups who could hold the key to a new government, as efforts intensified on all sides to avoid early polls, officials said on Thursday .

Sharma received Congress party president Sitaram Kesri at New Delhi's Presidential Palace. Kesri briefed him about his decision to back a new United Front government if Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda was replaced, officials said.

It was not clear if Kesri officially withdrew a letter he wrote to Sharma on March 31, staking his own claim to head a new government, a day after withdrawing support for Deve Gowda's minority coalition.
Earlier on Thursday, Sharma consulted Atal Behari Vajpayee, leader of the rightwing Hindu Bharatiya Janata (BJP), who is widely expected to gain, but not win outright, if elections are held soon.
Deve Gowda's 10-month old government was brought down by Congress and the BJP on April 11 when he lost a vote of confidence in parliament.
Vajpayee is believed to have asked Sharma to set up a new government soon, saying any further delay would only harm the nation.
Communist leader Harkishan Singh Surjeet also met Sharma to stress the need for Kesri to withdraw his claim to power before the United Front elected a new leader.

Surjeet's Communist Party of India-Marxist (CPI-M), which had earlier opposed any replacement of Deve Gowda, said on Wednesday that the issue could only be decided if Kesri first offically withdraws his claim.
A Congress spokesman said he was not aware if Kesri had withdrawn the letter to Sharma during their meeting.
"The letter is proving to be a stumbling block," a senior United Front official told reporters earlier on Thursday.
"The Left parties (in the coalition) have already asked the Congress to withdraw it. The other constituents also appreciate the Left stand and recognise the need for it," he said.
The official's comments followed several meetings between United Front Convener Chandrababu Naidu and Kesri to end the uncertainty triggered by the fall of Deve Gowda's government.
"There are problems which need to be sorted out," United Front spokesman Jaipal Reddy told reporters earlier on Thursday. "I am confident that all problems will be resolved."
Reddy said the 15-party coalition's decision-making Steering Committee would meet at 9.30 p.m. (1600 GMT) on Friday to elect a leader to replace Deve Gowda, ending a 19-day political crisis.
The 15-party alliance postponed a decision on who would replace Deve Gowda due to political infighting and the death of a veteran party boss, coalition leaders said.
Deve Gowda also attended the steering committee meeting on Thursday.
